title: How Many Pawns to BEAT Martin?
summary: Tony starts with only a king plus 1 pawn against Martin's full army, adding one pawn each game. Pawns start on the 2nd rank. He finally wins with 10 pawns, promoting and giving a two-queen ladder mate.
rules: White has only a king and N pawns; Black (Martin) has a full standard army.
Game 1: king + 1 pawn; add one pawn after every loss.
White pawns start on the second rank (filled in order, from a then onward is inferred).
Normal chess rules otherwise; pawns promote normally.
win_condition: Checkmate Martin; challenge ends at first win (took 10 pawns).

opponent.name: Martin
opponent.avatar_description: chess.com Martin bot: cartoon man with big dark beard, swept dark hair, smug half-smile, brown turtleneck

setup: Black full army; White Ke1 plus N pawns on rank 2. E.g. 10 pawns: rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/8/8/PPPPPPPP/2P1K1P1 w - - 0 1 (exact placement of pawns 9-10 not established; transcript says they started on the second rank)
